summary: Ryujo Yamada was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served as a professor at Tohoku University (attested 1953; emeritus attested 1972–1973) and head of Musashino University (attested 1963).

Ryuken Nawa works in Indology and Buddhist studies. His posts include lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2026.
Ryuken Sato specialized in Buddhist studies. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji (serving as sōgaku) and at Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Lausanne in 2003 under the supervision of Tom Tillemans.
Ryushin Kitao is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested in 2014 and 2026.

Ryūshin Saitō specializes in Buddhist studies. Affiliations include the Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2001), a professorship at Bukkyo University (attested 2015), and a faculty position at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Ryushin Sudo studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Taisho University around 1948–1953. He later held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Ryukoku University (ca. 1951–1956). He was affiliated with the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute in 1962 and served as professor at Kyoto Women's University from around 1972 to 1998.

Ryusho Hikata was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and later at Tohoku University. He was a professor and dean at Kyushu University and president of Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964).

Ryuta Kikutani specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020), and serves as an associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Ryutaro Tsuchida studied Indology at the University of Tokyo and completed doctoral studies at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1979–1983) before serving as professor and emeritus at the University of Tokyo.

Ryutoku Kimura studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Komazawa University (~1966–1973). He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1978), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichō-ji (attested 2003).
Ryuyu Saito is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyo Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Research Association.
Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Ryōmin Akizuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo around 1941–1944. He later served at Saitama Medical University from around 1973 to 1991.
Rüdiger Schmitt is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1958–1965). He held a post at Saarland University from around 1979 to 2004.

S. D. Laddu specialized in Indology and linguistics. He was associated with Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and served as Editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
S. G. F. Brandon studied religious studies and history/archaeology at the University of Leeds (~1930–1937). He later held a post at the University of Manchester from around 1951 to 1971.

S. Kuppuswami Sastri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Madras. He served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, Thiruvaiyaru, and later as professor at Presidency College and Annamalai University.
